title: Right anodyne maps are the maps lifting against right fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets and simplicial maps of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], in any fixed containing universe. A simplicial map $v:U\to V$ is right anodyne if and only if it has the left lifting property against every right fibration $q:E\to S$: for all simplicial maps $u:U\to E$ and $w:V\to S$ with $qu=wv$ there is a simplicial map $d:V\to E$ with $dv=u$ and $qd=w$. No quasicategory or Kan hypothesis is imposed on $U$, $V$, $E$ or $S$.

source.place: Definition 2.0.0.3 (right fibrations and right anodyne maps as the weakly saturated class of the right horns) with the small object argument of Appendix A.1.2; equivalently Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra (https://cisinski.app.uni-regensburg.de/CatLR.pdf), Section 4.1, before Corollary 4.1.10. Online sources, not archived; the exact numbered place is to be confirmed by the worker who splits this node (the creating review had no network access). Mathlib states the analogues for all horns and inner horns, not for right horns: SSet.anodyneExtensions_eq_retracts_transfiniteCompositions (AnodyneExtensions/Basic.lean:111-114) and SSet.innerAnodyneExtensions_eq_retracts_transfiniteCompositions (AnodyneExtensions/Inner/Basic.lean:89-93).

proof.text: For every generating right horn inclusion h:Λ_i^n→Δ^n with n≥1 and 0<i≤n, and every right fibration q:E→S, the defining right-fibration lifting property supplies a diagonal in every commutative square with left side h and right side q. Thus every generating right horn lies in the class L of maps having the left lifting property against all right fibrations.

The class L contains identities, is closed under composition and pushouts, and is closed under arrow retracts by the generic lifting-class closure statement [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. It contains every isomorphism $v:U\to V$: in a square $qu=wv$, take $d=u v^{-1}$, so $dv=u$ and $qd=wv v^{-1}=w$. Its closure under every small continuous transfinite composition follows from [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Since the right-anodyne class is, by definition, the smallest class containing isomorphisms and the generating right horns and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts, every right anodyne map belongs to L.

source.place: HTT Definition 2.0.0.3 (LLP definition), Appendix A.1.2, Proposition A.1.2.3 and Corollary A.1.2.7 (weak saturation and its identification with the LLP class).

proof.text: For the converse, apply the small-object factorization [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] in the category of small simplicial sets to the countable set $I=\{\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\mid n\geq1,\ 0<i\leq n\}$ with $\kappa=\aleph_0$; its hypotheses hold. Hom sets are small sets of compatible degreewise functions. Small colimits exist [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: in each degree take the disjoint union of the sets of the diagram modulo the relations imposed by its arrows; the simplicial operators descend, and the universal property holds degreewise. Each horn is a union of finitely many faces $\Delta^{n-1}$. A map from it to the colimit of an $\omega$-chain is given by the images of these finitely many simplices subject to finitely many face equations, so it factors through a finite stage; two such maps that agree in the colimit agree at a finite stage by the same finite argument. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_i^n,-)$ preserves these chain colimits. The cited factorization gives, for $v:U\to V$, a factorization $U\xrightarrow{i}W\xrightarrow{p}V$ with $i$ an $I$-cell map and $p$ having a diagonal filler in every square with left side in $I$.

source.place: HTT Appendix A.1.2, Proposition A.1.2.5, specialized to the set of right horn inclusions; the smallness check follows the existing DAG node lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-anodyne-factorization, step 1.

proof.text: The map $p$ is a right fibration: its lifting property against $I$ is exactly the right-fibration clause of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. The map $i$ is right anodyne by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]: it is a continuous transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of right horns, and a coproduct $\coprod_{a\in A}h_a$ of horn inclusions is obtained by well-ordering $A$ and attaching one summand at a time, a continuous transfinite composite of pushouts of single right horns whose colimit has the universal property of the coproduct pushout; the empty coproduct is an identity, an isomorphism. Now assume $v$ has the left lifting property against every right fibration. Apply it to the square with left side $v$, right side $p$, top map $i$ and bottom map $1_V$; it commutes since $pi=v$. It produces $s:V\to W$ with $sv=i$ and $ps=1_V$.

source.place: HTT Definition 2.0.0.3 and Appendix A.1.2, Corollary A.1.2.7 (cell maps lie in the weakly saturated class); the coproduct attachment follows the existing DAG node lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-anodyne-factorization, step 2.

proof.text: The equations s∘v=i and p∘s=1_V exhibit v as an arrow retract of i: the section square is (1_U,s), the retraction square is (1_U,p), and their composite is the identity square because p∘s=1_V. Right anodyne maps are closed under arrow retracts by [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], so v is right anodyne.

source.place: HTT Appendix A.1.2, Corollary A.1.2.7, together with the retract clause in the definition of weak saturation.

proof.text: The two implications use only the horn lifting clauses, the closure properties and the small-object factorization above. They do not require U, V, E or S to be quasicategories or Kan complexes, and the argument is valid in any fixed containing universe.

source.place: HTT Definition 2.0.0.3 and Appendix A.1.2, Proposition A.1.2.5; no quasicategory or Kan hypotheses are stated.
